questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me that the destination was English speaking. Secondly I wanted to go far away from home with nice weather.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UNSW had plenty of information before arrival, so it was easy to navigate in.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: If you arrived in a certain period you could get a transfer from the airport to wherever you were staying.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: If you go to UNSW live in Coogee! A lot of people from KU lived in a house with other international students (don't know what it's called). I lived in international housing I found through Flatmates and Flatmatefinder.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Live by the beach

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's difficult to get on campus housing when you are only staying 1 semester.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Sometimes it could take a long time to get courses approved for registration, but other than that it's quite easy trough their online system. 

Note the UNSW uses a trimester structure, so you have 1 winter course and 3 courses during the actual term. The courses in the winter term are very limited - 10 courses to choose from.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online system where you get approved different courses and in the end decide which 4 courses you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
They have a student hub that is open Monday-Friday, where you can get help. 
You can also write them emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful, but they are strict with prerequisites

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get easier courses so you can have fun and travel

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They course level was easier than KU, but you can definitely find courses that are as difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Very similar as there was lectures and tutorials
The grading system is very different - assignments, participation, homework, quizzes, tests, and exam all count for your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
COMM1000 - Creating Social Change
COMM1140 - Financial Management 
ECON2102  - Macroeconomics 2
ECON3110  - Development Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Development Economics is very interesting and the professor is very passionate and nice!

I know from other students that the Applied corporate finance course is really good but also very hard.

questions.answer:
Other fees are travelling, which is of course costly.

I didn't encounter any unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Alcohol in stores is very expensive, but same prices in the pub and club as in Denmark. 
Some foods are more expensive others cheaper, so I would say it equals out be the same price level as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a ton of different clubs you can join and they have a lot of advertising for it as well.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can think of

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The surf club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel the country - there are so many things to see in Australia

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - Aussies are super nice

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's kinda of difficult. The school is like 80% asians from either foreign or domestic students. Best way to socialize with Aussies are to join a club

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Didn't find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Have fun
Live in Coogee
Go surf

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Trimester structure
A lot of asians at the uni (some don't even speak English)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The travelling

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Structuring your free time and time spent on school - there are so many things to do in Sydney

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
